key_results: At 2 hours, both PBM groups showed significantly lower pain scores than sham (p < 0.05); 650 nm group had reduced analgesic consumption at 2 and 6 hours (p < 0.05); analgesic effect was transient, limited to acute phase
comments: Clinical trial design is rigorous but the transient nature of the effect and convergence by Day 2 limits practical clinical impact beyond immediate post-op management.

hypotheses.hypothesis: PBM reduces acute postoperative pain compared to sham control
hypotheses.result: Confirmed at 2 hours for both wavelengths (p < 0.05)

hypotheses.hypothesis: 650 nm wavelength provides superior early analgesic effect
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; reduced medication use at 2 and 6 hours vs sham

hypotheses.hypothesis: PBM improves overall oral health-related quality of life
hypotheses.result: Not confirmed; no significant overall difference, though 810 nm improved 'physical disability' domain

title: A velocity-informed framework for resolving functional stratification in rare human stem cells
task: Resolve functional heterogeneity in ultra-rare human stem cells using RNA velocity analysis
key_results: Velocity-informed framework identifies two kinetically distinct VSEL subsets: CD34⁺ fraction (deep quiescence) and CD133⁺ fraction (transcriptional priming toward lineage commitment); pathway analysis reveals state-specific stress response, metabolic regulation, and developmental gene networks
comments: Integration of RNA velocity with scRNA-seq provides functional insights into rare cell populations where direct functional assays are infeasible, enabling discovery of developmental trajectories.

model_io.model: very small embryonic-like stem cells (VSELs) from umbilical cord blood

hypotheses.hypothesis: VSELs comprise kinetically distinct quiescent and priming subsets with different developmental potentials
hypotheses.result: RNA velocity analysis reveals CD34⁺ deep quiescence and CD133⁺ lineage priming programs

title: SAMD4 represses VGLL4 mRNA to activate TEAD and promote cancer progression
task: Identify SAMD4 as repressor of VGLL4 mRNA to activate TEAD oncogenic program
key_results: SAMD4A/B destabilizes and represses VGLL4 mRNA translation, increasing TEAD activity and promoting cancer progression in vitro; SAMD4B inhibition elevates VGLL4, suppressing TEAD and cancer progression; transgenic liver-specific SAMD4B in Nf2-deficient mice accelerates intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (onset 1 week, death by 100 days)
comments: SAMD4 targeting represents an alternative approach to directly inhibiting YAP1/TAZ or TEAD, potentially circumventing resistance mechanisms to existing inhibitors.

hypotheses.hypothesis: SAMD4A/B promote TEAD activation by destabilizing VGLL4 mRNA
hypotheses.result: SAMD4 inhibition elevates VGLL4, suppressing TEAD and cancer progression

title: TFAM promotes mitochondrial division by increasing mitochondrial Sirt3
task: Elucidate TFAM role in mitochondrial division through Sirt3 interaction
key_results: TFAM overexpression promotes mitochondrial fragmentation; TFAM enhances Sirt3 mitochondrial localization and deacetylation activity; TFAM-Sirt3 interaction (via HMG-box A domain) activates AMPK/MFF/Drp1 pathway; high TFAM-SIRT3 co-expression correlates with better overall survival in KIRC
comments: Direct protein-protein interaction between TFAM and Sirt3 coordinates mitochondrial dynamics with NAD⁺-dependent deacetylation, linking bioenergetics to organellar remodeling.

hypotheses.hypothesis: TFAM promotes mitochondrial fission via direct Sirt3 interaction
hypotheses.result: HMG-box A deletion disrupts TFAM-Sirt3 binding, abolishing fission-promoting effects

title: PEX11 mediates intralumenal vesicle formation in peroxisomes
task: Characterize PEX11 isoform functions in peroxisomal intralumenal vesicle formation and size regulation
key_results: PEX11C/D/E promotes intralumenal vesicle formation, limits peroxisome size throughout development, required for fatty acid β-oxidation; PEX11A/B functions specifically during seedling lipid mobilization; complete PEX11 loss causes seedling lethality despite peroxisome abundance
comments: Functional diversification of PEX11 isoforms extends organellar roles beyond canonical division to internal membrane remodeling and developmental stage-specific regulation.

model_io.model: Arabidopsis pex11 null mutants with membrane/lumen reporters

hypotheses.hypothesis: PEX11 isoforms have distinct roles in peroxisomal membrane dynamics
hypotheses.result: PEX11C/D/E promote intralumenal vesicles throughout development; PEX11A/B function during seedling lipid mobilization

title: Oxidative stress causes a reversible decrease of deubiquitylases activity in old vertebrate brains
task: Characterize age-dependent loss of deubiquitylase activity through oxidative modification
key_results: Subset of cysteine protease DUBs progressively lose activity with age despite stable protein levels; oxidative stress impairs DUB function via thiol oxidation; antioxidant treatment (NACET) restores activity; DUB inhibition precedes proteasome decline; USP7 is among most age-affected DUBs
comments: Identification of redox-sensitive DUB inactivation as an early, reversible driver of aging-related proteostasis decline suggests therapeutic targets before point-of-no-return proteasome dysfunction.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Oxidative stress inactivates DUBs through thiol oxidation
hypotheses.result: Antioxidant treatment restores DUB activity in aged brains

title: Functional requirement for Dicer helicase arginine methylation in 26 G siRNA biogenesis and oocyte meiotic program
task: Define role of Dicer helicase arginine methylation in small RNA biogenesis and meiosis
key_results: DCR-1 GRARR motif arginine methylation (R495) enhances ERI-5/ERIC complex interaction; R495K mutation impairs 26G endo-siRNA production and oocyte meiosis; phenotype parallels DCR-1 catalytic domain phosphorylation mutants
comments: Coordinated post-translational modification of helicase and catalytic domains suggests allosteric regulation of Dicer conformation and complex assembly.

hypotheses.hypothesis: DCR-1 arginine methylation at R495 promotes ERI-5 interaction and 26G siRNA biogenesis
hypotheses.result: Asymmetric dimethylation of R495 enhances peptide-ERI-5 interaction; loss of R495 reduces interaction and impairs siRNA production

title: Mitochondrial respirasome-like supercomplexes support metabolic flexibility in yeast
task: Characterize metabolic flexibility supported by distinct respiratory supercomplex conformations
key_results: Engineered covalently-linked III₂IV₂ supercomplex supports robust respiratory activity; selectively impacts cytosolic NADH-driven respiration via distinct Nde1 interactions; tethered SC maintains metabolic flexibility
comments: The ability to decouple supercomplex formation from other variables reveals substrate-specific roles of different SC conformations in metabolic regulation.

model_io.model: engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae with tethered respiratory supercomplex

hypotheses.hypothesis: III₂IV₂ supercomplex configuration specifically impacts NADH-dependent respiration
hypotheses.result: Tethered SC preferentially affects Nde1-mediated NADH oxidation while maintaining FADH₂ respiration

title: NirFAP680: a highly bright and stable large Stokes shift near-infrared fluorogen-activating protein
task: Develop near-infrared fluorogen-activating protein (NirFAP680) for advanced biological imaging
key_results: NirFAP680 (NIR fluorogen HBMT + engineered NirFAP tag) shows 10-fold greater cellular brightness and superior photostability vs. current NIR FAPs; >100nm Stokes shift enables FRET/BRET applications; enables robust imaging in live cells and in vivo with single- and two-photon excitation
comments: Large Stokes shift combined with improved brightness and photostability represents significant technical advancement for multiplexed and deep-tissue imaging applications.

outputs: fluorescence emission (680 nm), improved signal-to-noise ratio

title: Astaxanthin suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma via targeting Wnt/Β-catenin pathway: Experimental study on chemically induced HCC in rats
task: Evaluate Wnt/β-catenin pathway inhibition by astaxanthin in chemically induced hepatocellular carcinoma
key_results: Combination astaxanthin + doxorubicin reduces ALT (45%), AST (35%), AFP (49%); downregulates Wnt/β-catenin components (FZD-7 -56%, LRP5/6 -62%, β-catenin -58%); upregulates GSK3β (41%), reduces cyclin D1 (46%); mitigates DOX-induced MDR1 upregulation (36% vs 65% monotherapy)
comments: Natural antioxidant combination therapy shows promise for reducing both HCC burden and chemotherapy-induced drug resistance through dual mechanisms.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Astaxanthin suppresses HCC through Wnt/β-catenin pathway inhibition
hypotheses.result: Combination therapy downregulates Wnt signaling components and cyclin D1, improving biomarkers and reducing nodules

title: γ-terpinene inhibits the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma by regulating the PTEN/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway mediated glycolysis
task: Determine mechanism of γ-terpinene anti-HCC activity via PTEN/PI3K/Akt pathway modulation
key_results: γ-terpinene dose-dependently inhibits HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion; upregulates PTEN and suppresses PI3K/Akt pathway; reduces glucose consumption by ~50%, ATP production and lactate generation; in vivo tumor suppression confirmed in xenografts
comments: Natural product targeting of glycolytic metabolism through phosphatase-mediated kinase pathway inhibition provides a rational approach to metabolic reprogramming in cancer.

hypotheses.hypothesis: γ-terpinene suppresses HCC through PTEN-dependent PI3K/Akt and glycolysis inhibition
hypotheses.result: PTEN inhibitor bpV reverses γ-terpinene effects, confirming PTEN as essential mediator

title: High-yield isolation and characterization of microvascular niche cells from human full-thickness skin biopsies
task: Develop protocol for isolation of primary microvascular niche cells from human skin
key_results: High-efficiency simultaneous isolation of dermal blood endothelial cells (HDBECs), lymphatic endothelial cells (HDLECs), fibroblasts, and pericytes from adult biopsies; cells form vascular-like networks in 3D fibrin gels
comments: This protocol enables generation of patient-matched, donor-specific vascular models that overcome limitations of immortalized or pooled cell sources.

inputs: isolated endothelial cells and support cells

title: Omacetaxine reduces c-Myc expression and demonstrates antitumor effects in osteosarcoma
task: Evaluate translation inhibitor omacetaxine against osteosarcoma via c-Myc reduction
key_results: Omacetaxine induces dose-dependent growth inhibition (IC50 nanomolar range) and apoptosis; reduces c-Myc protein levels across multiple OS cell lines; suppresses tumor growth and metastasis in orthotopic mouse models
comments: Translation inhibition as a strategy to target difficult-to-inhibit oncoprotein-driven cancers represents an alternative to direct kinase or protein-protein interaction inhibition.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Omacetaxine reduces c-Myc protein translation and downstream target expression
hypotheses.result: c-Myc protein and mRNA transcripts decreased; Myc target genes downregulated

title: Targeting the TLR4/NF-κB/TNF-α/MMP axis with dexamethasone attenuates glycocalyx degradation and restores microcirculatory perfusion in septic kidneys
task: Resolve TLR4/NF-κB/TNF-α/MMP pathway in sepsis-induced acute kidney injury pathogenesis
key_results: TLR4/NF-κB/TNF-α axis drives MMP-9/MMP-3 expression, degrading endothelial glycocalyx (HS, HA, CS, SDC1 increased) and disrupting tight junctions (ZO-1 decreased); dexamethasone suppresses pathway, restores glycocalyx integrity and renal perfusion (laser speckle imaging)
comments: Multi-omics integration (bulk RNA-seq, bioinformatics, in vitro and in vivo validation) provides strong mechanistic support for targeted anti-inflammatory intervention in septic AKI.

model_io.model: murine models of sepsis (CLP or LPS-induced)

hypotheses.hypothesis: TLR4/NF-κB/TNF-α/MMP axis mediates glycocalyx degradation in septic AKI
hypotheses.result: Dexamethasone suppresses pathway and restores glycocalyx integrity and renal perfusion

title: The transcription factor Rlm1 couples the MAPK Slt2/ERK1 pathway to the IRE1-driven unfolded protein response
task: Characterize crosstalk between MAPK and IRE1-UPR pathways
key_results: UPR operates in two phases: early phase through canonical IRE1 pathway, later phase additionally involves MAPK Slt2/ERK and MADS-box transcription factor Rlm1; Slt2 promotes IRE1 expression through Rlm1
comments: The identification of a two-phase UPR mechanism with MAPK-IRE1 crosstalk suggests hierarchical pathway organization that may be conserved in mammalian systems.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Slt2 promotes IRE1 expression through Rlm1
hypotheses.result: Confirmed through genetic and expression analysis

title: A conserved hormonal signalling–H2A.Z axis rapidly reorganizes 3D chromatin interactions in adipocyte thermogenesis
task: Characterize β3-AR signaling-driven chromatin reorganization via H2A.Z deposition in thermogenesis
key_results: β3-AR stimulation rapidly reorganizes chromatin loops within 4h; dynamically gained loops coupled to thermogenic gene activation; H2A.Z deposition enhances accessibility at loop anchors, facilitating MED1 recruitment; loss of H2A.Z impairs loop formation; brown fat H2A.Z deficiency impairs thermogenic activity and glucose tolerance; H2A.Z-occupied loops link to obesity-associated genetic variants
comments: Cross-species conservation of the β3-AR–H2A.Z–3D chromatin axis provides mechanistic and translational insights into metabolic control and genetic risk.

model_io.model: mouse and primary human brown adipocytes during β3-AR stimulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: β3-AR signaling rapidly reorganizes chromatin loops via H2A.Z deposition at loop anchors
hypotheses.result: H2A.Z loss impairs loop formation and thermogenic gene activation; H2A.Z deficiency reduces thermogenic capacity

title: TMEM87A suppresses ferroptosis and increases cancer immunotherapy resistance by maintaining the Golgi apparatus pH homeostasis
task: Identify role of TMEM87A in ferroptosis resistance and immunotherapy response
key_results: TMEM87A maintains Golgi pH homeostasis; ablation enhances antitumor T cell responses and potentiates PD1 blockade in multiple tumor models; negative correlation between TMEM87A expression and immunotherapy response in patients
comments: Strong link between organellar pH regulation and immunotherapy efficacy provides a mechanistic rationale for targeting ferroptosis suppressors in cancer.

model_io.model: murine tumor models (melanoma, colorectal, liver cancer)

hypotheses.hypothesis: TMEM87A buffers Golgi pH to suppress ferroptosis
hypotheses.result: TMEM87A ablation causes Golgi overacidification and ferroptosis sensitization

title: Chidamide synergizes with cisplatin-etoposide to trigger pyroptosis and anti-tumor immunity in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
task: Evaluate pyroptosis induction by HDAC inhibitor combined with chemotherapy in DLBCL
key_results: Chidamide synergizes with cisplatin-etoposide to trigger pyroptosis; enhances antitumor immune responses in DLBCL cells
comments: Combining epigenetic modulation with conventional chemotherapy to induce immunogenic cell death is a promising therapeutic strategy.

title: Enhancing inference of differential gene expression in metatranscriptomes from human microbial communities
task: Identify robust differential gene expression methods for metatranscriptomics using mock communities and real data
key_results: Benchmarking on mock communities (real, non-simulated data) outperforms simulated benchmarks; nominated method successfully inferred cross-feeding dynamics in gnotobiotic mice; per-organism sample filtering overcomes low-prevalence confounding
comments: Key insight: simulated data performance does not predict real-data robustness; real mock community benchmarking essential for metatranscriptomics method validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Simulated benchmarks accurately predict real-data differential expression method performance
hypotheses.result: Rejected; real mock community results diverged from simulated benchmarks

hypotheses.hypothesis: Per-organism prevalence and abundance filtering improves differential expression inference
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; enables valid inference in gnotobiotic and clinical datasets

title: Multivariate genetic analysis reveals three distinct pathological dimensions in musculoskeletal disorders
task: Dissect shared genetic architecture of musculoskeletal disorders via multivariate genetic modeling
key_results: Identified three distinct pathological factors explaining 48.27% total genetic variance; 795 genomic loci (136 novel), 273 candidate genes (20 interact with existing drugs); enrichment in brain-joint neural and gut-joint immune axes
comments: Novel approach using factor analysis to stratify heterogeneous disease; identifies distinct biological pathways for co-prevention strategies.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Musculoskeletal disorders share distinct genetic pathological factors with low genetic correlation
hypotheses.result: Three factors identified: degenerative, bone mass, and autoimmune, with minimal overlap

hypotheses.hypothesis: Brain-joint neural axis and gut-joint immune axis underlie distinct musculoskeletal pathology factors
hypotheses.result: Enrichment confirmed in embryonic brain and gut tissues; informs mechanistic understanding

title: The microbial metabolome: remodeling the therapeutic landscape in hematologic malignancies
task: Review microbial metabolome's role in drug efficacy and toxicity in hematologic malignancies
key_results: Demonstrates how gut microbial metabolites influence chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and transplant outcomes; identifies pathway toward metabolome-informed precision oncology
comments: Positions gut microbiome as actionable therapeutic target and biomarker source; bridges microbiome-oncology gap.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Microbial metabolites are causal drivers of treatment outcomes in hematologic malignancies
hypotheses.result: Review outlines evidence and pathway to precision oncology interventions

title: Personalized metabolite biomarker predictions reveal heterogeneous characteristics of Parkinson’s disease
task: Stratify Parkinson's disease patients via personalized metabolite biomarkers predicted from genome-scale metabolic models
key_results: TAMBOOR algorithm identified consensus PD biomarkers (dopamine, eumelanin, salsolinol, vitamin D3, retinal); stratified patients into three metabolically distinct clusters; revealed patient heterogeneity in well-known markers
comments: Personalized metabolite approach captures PD heterogeneity; highlights that consensus biomarkers may not apply uniformly across patients.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Personalized metabolite predictions reveal patient-specific PD subtypes
hypotheses.result: Three metabolically distinct patient clusters identified; stratification enables precision treatment

hypotheses.hypothesis: GEM-based metabolite analysis identifies disease mechanisms beyond consensus biomarkers
hypotheses.result: Cluster-specific metabolites (melatonin, biliverdin) show distinct secretion patterns despite absence from consensus

title: When normalization induces correlation: shared and unstable references can create hidden dependencies
task: Identify and quantify correlation inflation induced by shared-reference normalization transformations
key_results: Analytical derivation shows shared-reference normalization induces nonzero covariance even for independent variables; effect scales with reference variance; persists with increasing sample size
comments: Under-recognized preprocessing artifact with broad implications for omics correlation analyses; highlights importance of transformation-aware statistical inference.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Shared-reference transformations induce artificial correlation even for independent variables
hypotheses.result: Analytically proven; effect magnitude increases with reference variance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Sequential shared-reference transformations become unstable with variable denominators
hypotheses.result: Simulations and real-data analyses confirm heavy-tailed ratio effects and inflated correlations

title: Structural and genetic signatures of two classes of HCV E2 neutralizing face antibodies from non-human primates immunized with a recombinant E1E2
task: Characterize structural and genetic signatures of HCV E2 neutralizing antibodies from immunized non-human primates
key_results: NHP nAbs encoded by IGHV1-138*01 and IGHV4-NL_5*01 (human homologs IGHV1-69*10, IGHV4-59*12); recognize conserved E2 neutralizing face proximal to AR3; binding modes similar to human AR3-targeting nAbs
comments: Establishes NHP immunization as valid model for human HCV vaccine responses; germline similarities suggest conserved immune mechanisms.

model_io.model: Monoclonal nAb structural and genetic analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: NHP and human antibodies recognize conserved E2 epitopes via similar germline genes and binding modes
hypotheses.result: NHP AR3-targeting nAbs show structural homology to human AR3-targeting nAbs

title: Navigating multi-omic integration methods for human microbiome research
task: Review multi-omic integration methods for human microbiome research with focus on biological questions
key_results: Comprehensive landscape of multi-omic integration approaches; methods categorized by biological question (inter-omics interactions, molecular shifts in disease, patient stratification, mechanism inference)
comments: Timely review emphasizing that method selection should match biological question rather than adopting a one-size-fits-all approach.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Different multi-omic integration methods address distinct biological questions
hypotheses.result: Framework provided for matching methods to research objectives in microbiome studies

title: Benchmarking of shotgun sequencing depth reveals the potential and limitations of shallow metagenomics and strain-level analysis
task: Benchmark shotgun metagenomic sequencing depth for accurate taxonomic and functional profiling
key_results: Reference-based strain taxonomy accurate at 0.5–1.0 Gb; MAG reconstruction requires >10 Gb despite quality metrics (54.5–81.8% strain accuracy); functional pathways reliable at 2 Gb; proteome coverage requires ≥10 Gb
comments: Critical benchmark showing high-quality MAGs can be chimeric; challenges adequacy of standard metrics and emphasizes depth requirements for strain resolution.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Shallow metagenomics (<2 Gb) insufficient for accurate MAG-based strain-level analysis
hypotheses.result: MAG reconstruction requires >10 Gb; quality metrics inflate accuracy claims (54.5–81.8% actual strain recovery)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Functional and taxonomic depth requirements differ substantially
hypotheses.result: Pathways resolved at 2 Gb; full proteome coverage requires ≥10 Gb

title: Epigenetic fingerprints link early-onset colon and rectal cancer to pesticide exposure
task: Link early-onset colorectal cancer to pesticide exposure via epigenetic methylation risk scores
key_results: Herbicide picloram identified as novel EOCRC risk factor (discovery P=4.4×10⁻⁴, replication P=3.1×10⁻³); validated in population-based 21-year US county data (P=4.52×10⁻⁴); association persists after socioeconomic adjustment
comments: Clever use of methylation scores as exposome proxies; real-world validation across cohorts and ecological data strengthens causality inference.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Picloram exposure is causally associated with EOCRC risk
hypotheses.result: Discovered in methylation analysis (P=4.4×10⁻⁴), replicated across 9 cohorts (P=3.1×10⁻³), and validated ecologically (P=4.52×10⁻⁴)

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the sponge Halisarca dujardinii
task: Chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of regenerative sponge Halisarca dujardinii
key_results: 226.5 Mbp nuclear assembly with 21 chromosome-scale scaffolds (N50 10.1 Mbp); 14 mitochondrial protein-coding genes; 14,565 nuclear genes (85.6% annotated) with refined 3′ UTRs from bulk/scRNA-seq
comments: High-quality reference genome for regeneration research; integration of single-cell RNA-seq substantially improves gene annotation accuracy.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Chromosome-level assembly and scRNA-seq integration enable accurate sponge genome annotation
hypotheses.result: 14,565 genes annotated with refined 3′ UTRs; high-quality reference for regeneration studies

title: An Open Dataset for the Acoustic Monitoring of Nocturnal Migratory Birds in Europe
task: Acoustic monitoring and taxonomic classification of nocturnal migratory bird vocalizations
key_results: NBM dataset contains 13,359 annotated vocalizations from 117 Western Palearctic species; two-stage deep object detection achieves competitive accuracy on 45 most common species
comments: Crowdsourced annotation enables large-scale passive monitoring of difficult-to-track nocturnal species; audio detection pipeline smaller than required for similar visual systems.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Crowdsourced effort can produce high-quality vocalization annotations enabling automated species detection

title: A multi-modal dataset for insect biodiversity with imagery and DNA at the trap and individual level
task: Automated taxonomic classification of bulk insect samples combining DNA barcoding with image segmentation
key_results: MassID45 dataset with 17,000+ annotated specimens; combines molecular and imaging data at sample and individual levels for biodiversity monitoring
comments: Addresses practical ecological survey challenges by handling unsorted bulk samples rather than individual specimens, advancing tiny object detection benchmarks.

hypotheses.result: Framework validated; dataset released for ML and ecological research

title: Causal relationship between autoimmune diseases and iron deficiency anemia: a two-sample mendelian randomization study
task: Infer causal relationships between autoimmune diseases and iron deficiency anemia via bidirectional Mendelian randomization
key_results: IVW analysis reveals significant IDA risk increases from rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, ulcerative colitis; suggestive associations for ankylosing spondylitis, celiac disease, Crohn's disease, systemic lupus erythematosus
comments: MHC region removal is critical for specificity; results support causal (not merely associational) links between specific autoimmune diseases and IDA.

title: Accurate classification and prediction of knee osteoarthritis based on Al-Biruni Earth Radius metaheuristic optimizer and LSTM classifier
task: Classify knee osteoarthritis using hybrid Al-Biruni Earth Radius-LSTM optimizer with deep learning
key_results: Google-BER-LSTM achieves 0.9953 accuracy, 0.9387 precision, 0.9708 NPV, 0.9454 F-score on KOA dataset; outperforms 10 comparative optimizers (HHO, JAYA, SBO, GSA, SFS, MVO, BBO, WOA, PSO, TSH)

hypotheses.result: Achieved 0.9953 accuracy, outperforming 10 alternative optimizers

title: Modeling the impact of community information dissemination on the transmission dynamics of lymphatic filariasis
task: Model transmission dynamics of lymphatic filariasis incorporating community awareness and mosquito populations
key_results: Fitted deterministic model to Ghana data (NMSE 0.0285); sensitivity analysis shows awareness rate (κ) critically reduces transmission; integrated control strategies outperform individual interventions
comments: Demonstrates that information dissemination is a quantifiable transmission reduction factor; provides data-driven support for public health messaging.

hypotheses.result: Sensitivity analysis confirmed awareness rate (κ) as critical control parameter

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integrated control (awareness + treatment + mosquito control) outperforms single interventions

title: Scale adaptive and robust intrinsic dimension estimation via optimal neighbourhood identification

key_results: Protocol identifies optimal scale range where ID is meaningful; self-consistent approach based on constant density assumption; demonstrated robustness to noise

hypotheses.result: Protocol validated on artificial and real-world datasets; demonstrates noise robustness

title: MEAST: a novel framework for analyzing gene set stability in single cell transcriptomics
task: Assess gene set activity stability in single-cell RNA-seq via modular scoring and genetic algorithm optimization
key_results: MEAST framework combines truncated SVD with genetic algorithm for gene set scoring; accurately distinguishes cell subtypes in blood scRNA-seq; identifies core active genes, eliminating low-activity genes
comments: Addresses practical challenge of variable gene set member contributions; stability assessment and explainability provide advantages over simpler scoring methods.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stability assessment identifies reproducible, high-contributing gene set members
hypotheses.result: Framework effectively eliminated low-activity genes in scRNA-seq data

title: HybridViT-CAB: a vision transformer and convolutional attention network for precision weed detection in agricultural systems
task: Detect and classify agricultural weeds using hybrid vision transformer-convolutional attention architecture
key_results: ViT-CAB hybrid achieves AUC 0.97; ViT alone reaches 91% accuracy; hybrid offers superior per-class balance and Grad-CAM interpretability; 412 K parameters, 141 ms/image for real-time deployment
comments: Demonstrates trade-off between accuracy and interpretability; hybrid architecture balances performance with explainability for practical precision agriculture.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hybrid ViT-CAB architecture provides superior class-balanced performance and interpretability vs. ViT alone
hypotheses.result: AUC 0.97 with balanced per-class predictions; Grad-CAM visualizations validate focus on relevant regions

key_results: TCMNet achieves 91.59% FROC score on LUNA16 dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art; dynamic tanh improves feature stability; cascaded attention enhances multi-scale interaction
comments: Addresses practical detection challenges (small nodules, complex structures) through modified attention mechanisms; strong performance on benchmark dataset.

title: Identification of potential MenT3 inhibitors for Mycobacterium tuberculosis using the generative artificial intelligence and SilicoXplore platform
task: Identify MenT3 inhibitors for tuberculosis through generative AI and virtual screening

hypotheses.result: Five candidates identified with favorable binding stability and thermodynamic properties

task: Optimize cholera control via stochastic adaptive modeling incorporating asymptomatic transmission

title: Uncovering core diseases in temporal trajectories of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome in UK Biobank: network-based study

key_results: Swin Transformer achieves 98% accuracy in grain counting, outperforming ResNet-50 and DINO; Grad-CAM and LIME provide interpretability; robust across morphological parameters
comments: Demonstrates practical application of modern vision transformers with explainability; comprehensive statistical validation supports generalizability.

title: Cohort vs case–control design for transformer-based prediction of asthma exacerbations in mild asthma
task: Compare cohort vs. case-control study designs for transformer-based prediction of asthma exacerbations
key_results: Case-control AUC 0.85 vs. cohort 0.70–0.71; both designs generalize across health systems; calibration differs substantially between designs
